presentingComplaint: Found collapsed in his field with copious frothing at the mouth and difficulty breathing after suspected pesticide ingestion.
history: Agricultural worker brought in ~45 minutes after deliberate ingestion of an unlabelled organophosphate insecticide (chlorpyrifos-type) following a family dispute. Empty pesticide container found beside him. Rapid onset of profuse salivation, lacrimation, vomiting, diarrhoea, urinary incontinence and progressive breathlessness. Clothing soaked and reeking of a solvent/garlic-like odour. No prior psychiatric history documented; no chronic illness, not on regular medication.
examination: Confused and agitated, then progressively drowsy. Pinpoint pupils (miosis) poorly reactive to light. Profuse salivation and lacrimation, drenching sweat. Bilateral coarse crepitations with audible wheeze and copious bronchial secretions on auscultation. Diffuse muscle fasciculations over face and limbs; generalised weakness. Bowel sounds hyperactive, urinary and faecal incontinence. Pertinent negatives: no focal neurological deficit, no neck stiffness, no rash, skin not dry (contrasts with anticholinergic toxidrome).

labs.ABG: pH 7.28, respiratory + metabolic acidosis, PaO2 62 mmHg on room air
labs.ECG: sinus bradycardia, prolonged QTc, no ischaemic changes

imaging: Chest X-ray: bilateral patchy alveolar shadowing consistent with excess bronchial secretions / early aspiration; heart size normal.
finalDiagnosis: Acute organophosphate (anticholinesterase) poisoning with cholinergic crisis
citations: Harrison 22e — Poisoning and Drug Overdose (cholinesterase inhibitors / insecticides)
stewardship: not applicable — non-infective. Management is antidotal: atropine titrated to drying of secretions plus pralidoxime (oxime), airway protection, and decontamination.
contraindications: Avoid suxamethonium — prolonged paralysis due to plasma cholinesterase inhibition
Withhold oximes only if a pure carbamate is confirmed; otherwise give with atropine
edgeCases: Intermediate syndrome (proximal/neck-flexor and respiratory-muscle weakness) 24-96h after apparent recovery
Delayed organophosphate-induced peripheral neuropathy weeks later
Carbamate poisoning gives a similar but shorter, self-limiting toxidrome
Massive lipophilic OP ingestion can cause recurrent/relapsing cholinergic crisis over days
expectedMaiK: Miosis with muscarinic overdrive (SLUDGE), bronchorrhoea, fasciculations and bradycardia after pesticide exposure define a cholinergic crisis from anticholinesterase poisoning; secure the airway, give escalating atropine titrated to dried secretions, add pralidoxime, and decontaminate. Confirm with low plasma/RBC cholinesterase but do not delay antidotes for the result.
expectedNextQuestions: What exact pesticide/compound was ingested and how much, and was it an organophosphate or carbamate?
Are secretions drying and is the chest clearing after each atropine dose (atropinisation endpoint)?
expectedInvestigations: Arterial blood gas and serial oxygenation/ventilation assessment
ECG (QTc, bradyarrhythmia) and continuous cardiac monitoring
